meta.assessor: Application security assessment — deliverable 3 of docs/TEST_BRIEF.md

findings.description: All four desktop agent builds are unsigned. `agent/build/signing.py` is written for signing and reads `SENTINEL_MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY` / `SENTINEL_WINDOWS_SIGN_THUMBPRINT`, and `.github/workflows/agent-build.yml` already passes the secrets — but no certificates exist, so `sign()` returns `signed=False`. The manifest records it and the download page renders it, quoting the Gatekeeper/SmartScreen dialog verbatim before the click, which is the right handling of the constraint. It is still a user being trained to click past an OS warning to install a process that reads their machine and holds a long-lived credential.
findings.exploitation: Two paths. (1) A user who has learned to dismiss 'unidentified developer' for the real agent dismisses it for a substituted one; with no signature there is nothing for the OS to compare. (2) The download page publishes a sha256 per build — the only integrity check available — and it is served by the same origin as the binary, so an attacker who can alter one alters both.
findings.impact: An attacker who can modify the published artifact or intercept its delivery gets code execution on every monitored machine, as a service that starts at boot. The agent's own trust boundary — opaque revocable tokens, a 0600 config, never a password — would not survive it.
findings.fix: Obtain an Apple Developer ID and an EV/OV Authenticode certificate and set the secrets the workflow already reads; no code changes are needed. Until then, publish the manifest's sha256 values somewhere this API does not serve, so the hash is not vouched for by the same channel as the file.
findings.status: Open — blocked on a certificate, not on code

findings.description: `backend/.env.ci` and `backend/.env.test` each carry two database URLs with passwords. The JWT signing keys they used to hold are gone — generated per run by the Makefile, the composite CI action and `tests/conftest.py` instead — which removes the part that was genuinely a credential. What remains is `sentinel`/`sentinel_app`, which is what `docker-compose.yml` publishes to create the local database in the first place, on roles that exist only for databases `make e2e-db` drops and recreates. `backend/.env` — the real JWT secret, the VAPID keypair and the Gmail App Password — is gitignored and has never been committed, confirmed against the full history.
findings.exploitation: None. The credentials authenticate to a local development database whose own compose file declares the same values, and the roles have no existence outside it.
findings.impact: None. A true positive for the pattern, and not a credential in any meaningful sense.
findings.fix: Removing them would mean generating a role password and threading it through `create_database.py`, migration 0001's `CREATE ROLE`, Alembic and the server across separate `make` invocations — real fragility in the stack four test suites depend on, to hide a value `docker-compose.yml` has to publish anyway. `.github/workflows/security-review.yml` allow-lists these two paths with the reason inline, so a secret in a third file is still a failure.
findings.status: Open — accepted; the signing keys were removed, the compose credentials remain

findings.type: Row-level security not forced for the owner role on 14 tables (CWE-266)
findings.exposure: Internal — requires a code change to reach
findings.description: Migration 0016 applies `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` to the nine tenant tables no owner-role path touches, so the table owner is now subject to the policies there. Fourteen cannot join them, and the reason is architectural rather than an oversight: signup and login must read `users` and `refresh_tokens` before an identity exists; `/enroll` is authenticated by the code itself and writes `enrollment_codes`, `devices` and `agent_tokens`; the ingest socket authenticates a *device* and writes the six metric tables; and four workers each enumerate one table to discover which tenants to sweep.
findings.exploitation: Requires a code change, not a request. `tests/test_unscoped_import_guard.py` walks the AST of `app/` and fails the build on any new use of the owner session, with a seven-entry allow-list each carrying its reason. `tests/test_rls_force.py` records which fourteen tables are exempt and why, so adding one to the forced list fails with the explanation rather than at runtime in a worker nobody is watching.
findings.impact: None reachable. Recorded so the split is a documented decision rather than an accident.
findings.fix: No further action. The remaining fourteen cannot be forced without breaking the paths named above; the AST guard is the control that covers them.
findings.status: Informational — the forceable nine are forced; the rest are tested and documented

findings.type: Pickle as a model serialisation format (CWE-502)
findings.exposure: Requires both a local write and this deployment's secret
findings.description: `joblib.load` is pickle, and unpickling executes arbitrary code in the API process. Two controls stand in front of it now. `_only_owner_can_write()` refuses a model file, or a directory, that any other local account could write. `model_integrity.verify()` then checks a detached HMAC-SHA256 sidecar keyed on a value derived from this deployment's own secret, before the bytes reach the unpickler — so a file an attacker did manage to write, by a permissions drift or a restored backup, is refused rather than executed. A missing sidecar is a failure, not a pass.
findings.exploitation: Not reachable. An attacker would need both a write into the operator's model directory and the deployment's signing key — and anyone holding the latter can already mint an access token for any account, so the model file would be the harder path, not the easier one.
findings.impact: None reachable. The residual is that the format is still code rather than data.
findings.fix: No further action while models are written by the local training script and read by the same machine. If they ever need to move between machines, replace joblib with a format that is not code — skops, ONNX, or the forest's parameters as JSON. An HMAC proves provenance, not safety.
findings.status: Informational — provenance and permissions both enforced

domains.evidence: Argon2id with parameters pinned in settings. Refresh rotation with reuse detection confirmed live — a replay 401s and the rotated token dies with the family. Nine JWT forgeries all refused. No user enumeration by response body or by timing (28ms vs 28ms, ratio 1.02). Signup screens commonly guessed passwords offline; login deliberately does not, so the policy cannot be read off the endpoint. The two cookie-authenticated routes now carry a second layer behind SameSite=strict: a browser announcing a cross-site request is refused on `Sec-Fetch-Site`, a header page JavaScript cannot forge.
domains.deductions: The breached-password screen is a curated list rather than a full corpus — an offline check, chosen so signup does not depend on a third party being reachable.

domains.evidence: RLS with a policy on all 23 tenant tables, verified against the live database. Migration 0016 forces it for the owner role on the nine tables no owner-role path touches. All 46 protected operations refuse an anonymous caller; a second tenant was denied on every cross-tenant probe, every one a 404 with the victim's data intact. The owner session is policed by an AST-walking test with a seven-entry allow-list.
domains.deductions: SEC-003 — fourteen tables cannot be forced, because the pre-auth paths, the ingest socket and four workers legitimately read them through the owner role.

domains.evidence: No dynamic SQL takes user input: the four places a table name is a string interpolate from frozen module constants, each traced individually. 8 payload families x 4 endpoints produced no 5xx and no reflection. 10 traversal payloads across two handlers all refused. The web-push endpoint is validated as a request target at the schema and re-checked by resolution before the send. The ingest frame parser — the one place an untrusted machine's bytes meet a schema — carries 47 fuzz tests asserting no input produces anything but a clean ValidationError.

Seven security headers on every response including 404s, static files and binary downloads. HSTS correctly scheme-gated. CORS reflects no arbitrary origin. The server binds loopback, so the Funnel's https:// front door is the only way in. Both WebSocket handshakes check Origin before the ticket is read. The CSP carries no 'unsafe-inline' anywhere — verified in a browser against five live charts streaming from a real agent, with an injected <style> element and setAttribute('style') both refused.

backend/.env has never been committed. Opaque tokens are 256-bit, sha256 at rest, looked up by unique index. The agent token file is 0600 through a verified descriptor. The access token never touches disk in either client. Every signing key published in this repository is refused in production. The CI and test signing keys are generated per run rather than committed, and the agent-download ticket moved from a query string — where a URL leaks into access logs and history — into an HttpOnly, SameSite=strict cookie.
domains.deductions: SEC-002 — the two CI env files still carry docker-compose's own published database passwords.

domains.evidence: **Zero known vulnerabilities in every manifest**: 80 pinned backend packages, the agent's 23, and all five JavaScript projects. The pinned closure is what makes that mean anything. The release APK is signed with a real key and `make mobile-apk` refuses to fall back to React Native's public debug key. The build manifest is validated, not trusted.
domains.deductions: SEC-001 — four unsigned desktop binaries, blocked on a certificate rather than on code.

domains.evidence: UserOut has no password_hash field to exclude. Metric data is never interpreted as an instruction. FCM tokens redacted before logging. No report stored server-side. Novelty models are permission-checked and HMAC-verified against this deployment's own key before any unpickle.
domains.deductions: SEC-004 — the serialisation format is still code rather than data, which matters only if models are ever made portable.

domains.evidence: `ENVIRONMENT` is required with no default, so a deployment that never considered it fails at startup naming the field rather than running unvalidated. The validator then enforces six requirements including every signing key published in this repository. /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json all 404 in production. X-Forwarded-For is trusted only from the local proxy — six spoofing attempts failed to escape a rate-limit bucket. The default bind is loopback.

No stack trace, ORM name or filesystem path in any error body. No Server banner. Secrets redacted before logging. The rate limiter degrades to a per-process counter on a Redis outage rather than removing the limit, and says so in the log.
domains.deductions: Nothing on this deployment alerts on the fail-open log line — an operational task the code cannot do for itself.

domains.evidence: 1197 tests green across five runners: 777 backend, 188 agent, 80 web, 95 mobile JS, 57 Kotlin. 421 Selenium and 560 Appium cases cover the authenticated surface — both suites re-run and passing against the final dependency and code state. The ingest parser has a dedicated fuzz suite. SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning and live API security checks run on every push and pull request, failing only on Critical.
